about.title: About
about.headline: Engineer first. Architect by trade. Author by circumstance.
about.bio_intro: I am a Principal Cloud Solutions Architect and AWS Subject Matter Expert with more than ten years in AWS platform engineering, security and DevOps, and six AWS certifications including Solutions Architect Professional and Security Specialty. I design and deliver multi-account landing zones, zero-trust network perimeters, production Kubernetes platforms, multi-region disaster recovery and agentic AI platforms for enterprise and regulated clients — a European institution, Volkswagen, a global gaming publisher, an FCA-regulated fintech, public-sector utilities and IoT companies.
about.bio_current: Since 2025 I work independently through Aspect Solutions from Tavira, Portugal, usually embedded as the principal architect inside a client's platform or consulting team. I care about ownership boundaries, least privilege, change management that engineers actually follow, and designs that survive a live failover drill.
about.bio_personal: I am also an author. My memoir Honor Bound was published by Simon & Schuster in 2012, and Un passo fuori dalla notte by Longanesi in 2015. Off the clock: manga, long walks on the Algarve coast, and gothic architecture.
about.case_text: Between 2007 and 2015 I was wrongfully accused in the Meredith Kercher case in Perugia and spent almost four years in prison before Italy's Supreme Court of Cassation definitively acquitted me on 27 March 2015. I completed my master's degree while the proceedings were still open and have worked continuously in software and cloud engineering since. I do not hide that chapter and I do not lead with it: the facts, a timeline and the court documents are on a dedicated page.

I have lived through events most people only read about; they taught me patience, the value of evidence and the cost of standing by the truth. I bring the same determination to systems that have to protect, scale and endure.

honor.meta: With Andrew Gumbel · Simon & Schuster · September 2012 · English · ISBN 978-1-4516-9600-4
honor.synopsis: Accused of one of the most publicised murders of our time, targeted by the media and sentenced by the courts, Raffaele Sollecito spent four years in prison for a crime he had nothing to do with. Written after his 2011 appeal acquittal, Honor Bound is his first-person account of the arrest, the trials, the years in Terni prison, and why he refused to save himself by turning on Amanda Knox.
honor.quote: He refused to testify against her to save his own skin, because he knew she would be lost forever.

case.title: The Case
case.headline: The Meredith Kercher case, 2007–2015
case.lede: On the night of 1 November 2007, Meredith Kercher, a 21-year-old British student, was murdered in Perugia, Italy. I was 23, a computer-science student in the same city, and had been dating Amanda Knox for a week. Five days later we were both arrested. I spent almost four years in prison for a crime I had nothing to do with. On 27 March 2015, Italy's Supreme Court of Cassation definitively acquitted us both.
case.respect: Meredith's family lost a daughter and a sister. Nothing on this page is meant to diminish that, and I have never treated my acquittal as anything other than a return to the truth.

t2007.text: Arrested in Perugia together with Amanda Knox, five days after the murder. Held in pre-trial detention at Terni prison.

t2009.text: Convicted at first instance by the Perugia Court of Assizes (Massei court) and sentenced to 25 years.

t2011.text: Acquitted on appeal by the Perugia Court of Assizes of Appeal (Hellmann court) after independent experts found the DNA evidence unreliable. Released after 1,427 days in prison.

t2013.text: The Supreme Court of Cassation annuls the appeal acquittal and orders a new appeal trial in Florence.

t2014.text: Re-convicted by the Florence Court of Assizes of Appeal (Nencini court) and sentenced to 25 years.

t2015.text: The Supreme Court of Cassation (Fifth Criminal Section) definitively acquits both defendants. The written reasoning, published in September 2015, cites serious investigative failures and the absence of any biological trace of either defendant in the room where the crime took place. Under Italian law the ruling is final.

q1.a: Yes. On 27 March 2015 Italy's Supreme Court of Cassation definitively acquitted Raffaele Sollecito and Amanda Knox of the murder of Meredith Kercher. A Cassation acquittal is final under Italian law: there is no further appeal and no retrial.

q2.q: How long was he in prison?
q2.a: Almost four years — 1,427 days of pre-trial detention at Terni prison, from 6 November 2007 to 3 October 2011, when he was acquitted on appeal and released. The 2014 re-conviction never led to a return to prison and was annulled in 2015.

q3.q: Who was convicted of the murder?
q3.a: Rudy Guede was convicted of the murder of Meredith Kercher in separate, fast-track proceedings. His conviction became final in December 2010 with a 16-year sentence.

q4.q: What did the Supreme Court say in 2015?
q4.a: The Court's written reasoning, published in September 2015, described the investigation as marked by serious failures and noted that no biological trace of Sollecito or Knox was found in the room where the crime occurred, whereas Guede's traces were. It closed the case with a full acquittal rather than an acquittal for insufficient evidence.

q5.q: Was he compensated for the wrongful detention?
q5.a: No. In 2017 the Florence Court of Appeal rejected his claim for compensation for the years spent in pre-trial detention. He has continued to campaign for reform of the Italian justice system.

q6.q: Does the case affect his professional work?
q6.a: No. He completed his MSc in Software Engineering at the University of Verona in 2014, while the proceedings were still open, and has worked continuously in software and cloud engineering since — today as a Principal Cloud Solutions Architect with six AWS certifications. Clients and employers have always had access to these facts.

q7.q: Where can I read the court documents?
q7.a: The rulings, appeal decisions and expert reports are published on this site's Documents page, mostly in the original Italian.

q8.a: Yes — two memoirs: Honor Bound (Simon & Schuster, 2012, written with Andrew Gumbel) and Un passo fuori dalla notte (Longanesi, 2015).

antonella.name: Antonella Petruzzella
antonella.quote: I met Raffaele in our first year of high school — he has always been a pleasant, generous and friendly person. One day he told me that every action must be driven by a feeling of love and affection, that love is the feeling at the root of everything. That day I understood that there are people who still believe in these important values. Raffaele is one of the most genuine and sincere people I have ever known and I am proud to be his friend.

francesco.name: Francesco Marrano
francesco.quote: I grew up with Raffaele — that's why we feel like brothers. Many important experiences of our lives we lived together, starting from nursery school! We grew up and found ourselves together again in high school. We started traveling together — Barcelona, Lisbon. Raffaele and I share a plan to spend a month in Japan, because we are united by many interests like manga and technology. I hope this terrible story ends soon because Raffaele is a fantastic person who doesn't deserve all this pain.

erica.name: Erica Milillo
erica.quote: I called him the Little Lord for his elegance, delicacy, his sense of respect for everyone! When a friend is far away because of something that leaves everyone with a bitter taste and makes you feel powerless, it's a bit hard to bring out that smile of joy... but the memories with Raffaele are only memories of joy. This is Raffaele for me — A Prince of Great Nobility of Soul!

milko.name: Milko Desantis
milko.quote: My knowledge of Raffaele goes back many years: we attended middle school and high school together — the years that in my opinion are the ones in which friendships are created that then remain for a lifetime. And so it is.

memories.name: Memories IT Company
memories.tagline: "La memoria è la poetica del ricordo." — Alessandro Morandotti
memories.description: Founded and led a web agency that built innovative digital products for clients across Italy. Memories IT Company was the umbrella under which I developed two main web applications — SunTickets and BeOnMemories — alongside client projects ranging from social marketplaces to real-time trading platforms. This is where I honed my full-stack engineering skills and discovered my passion for building scalable systems.

suntickets.name: SunTickets®
suntickets.description: An innovative online booking and management platform designed for beach clubs, swimming pools, resorts, campsites, villages, and restaurants. SunTickets combined a comprehensive management system with a revolutionary booking experience — users could book umbrellas, sunbeds, tables, pitches or any spot by clicking directly on an aerial photo of the venue (captured by drones when not available).

beonmemories.name: BeOnMemories
beonmemories.description: An innovative memorial web platform that let users honor their loved ones from anywhere. Users could purchase roses, candles, votive objects, and floral arrangements, and have a courier deliver them directly to the tombstone — all through an intuitive online experience. The platform featured a comprehensive database of cemeteries across Italy, making it easy to locate any grave and arrange a delivery without having to travel in person.
